subject: How to eliminate unwanted line breaks

messages.author: 171793e5bd0cb49f
messages.subject: How to eliminate unwanted line breaks
parts:
Hello R enthusiasts.

I have some hand-me-down corpus files that have unwanted line breaks
in the middle of sentences. I used the function paste(file, collapse="
") to eliminate those line breaks and put line-final words next to
line-initial words, in preparation for retrieving bigrams. However,
when I use the function strsplit(file, sep="[.,?!]") to break up the
single-element vector (which has 700,000 words), it never finishes
working, at least not after seven hours, when I stopped it.

I discovered the following warning about strsplit() in the manual:
"The standard regular expression code has been reported to be very
slow when applied to extremely long character strings (tens of
thousands of characters or more): the code used when perl = TRUE seems
much faster and more reliable for such usages." With a corpus file of
700,000 words, it was little wonder why it never finished the
operation.

Does anyone have any words of wisdom on how to put line-final words
back together with line-initial words in preparation for retrieving
bigrams in a file with 700,000 words?

Thanks. Earl Brown

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] How to eliminate unwanted line breaks
parts:
Well, I would do something like this:

# load tagged Brown corpus
x.1 <- scan(file.choose(), what=character(0), sep="\n", quote="",
comment.char="")

# take the time
date()
# [1] "Thu Oct 15 22:06:06 2009"

# split up into 'words'
x.2 <- unlist(strsplit(x.1, "[^-a-zA-Z']+", perl=TRUE))

# take the time again
date()
# [1] "Thu Oct 15 22:06:10 2009"
# i.e., this takes 4 seconds on my laptop ...

# check result
head(x.2, 40)
[1] "" "SA" "the" "AT"
[5] "Fulton" "NP" "County" "NN"
[9] "Grand" "JJ" "Jury" "NN"
[13] "said" "VBD" "Friday" "NR"
[17] "an" "AT" "investigation" "NN"
[21] "of" "IN" "Atlanta's" "NP"
[25] "recent" "JJ" "primary" "NN"
[29] "election" "NN" "produced" "VBD"
[33] "no" "AT" "evidence" "NN"
[37] "that" "CS" "any" "DTI"

# 1 million words plus their tags:

I am not sure why 700K words should be a problem ;-)

messages.subject: Re: How to eliminate unwanted line breaks
parts:
What happens when you first collapse all elements of the vector into
one element, in order to put back together bigrams that were once in
the same intonation unit (that is, between punctuation that marks
pauses .,?!, etc.) but have since inadvertently been separated by line
breaks? My file looks like it was copied from a webpage and then
pasted into a word processor, and thus line breaks were inserted at
the end of each (visual) line from the webpage. Because of this, I
collapsed all vector elements into one element and then tried to split
it up at the punctuation marks that represent pauses, but it never
finished, I assume because the one vector element had 700,000 words.
I'm trying to preserve the pauses that are marked with punctuation
before getting the bigrams, if possible. Thanks again for your help.

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: How to eliminate unwanted line breaks
parts:
> What happens when [...]
I am not sure what you mean by "What happens when [...]" but a rather
inelegant solution to this problem is this (again using the Brown
corpus, which is 40% larger than your corpus:

###########################
# load Brown corpus tagged, strip tags, strip line numbers
x.1 <- scan("/home/stgries/Corpora/ICAME2/BROWN_tagged_brownscheme/BTL.TXT",

x.1 <- gsub("_[^ ]+", "", x.1, perl=T)
x.1 <- sub("^.*? ", "", x.1, perl=T)

# take time
date()

x.2 <- gsub("([\\.\\?\\!\\:])", "\\1\n", x.1, perl=TRUE) # look for
punctuation marks
x.3 <- paste(x.2, collapse=" ") # collapse with line break
output.file <- "temp.txt" # define temporary output file
cat(x.3, file=output.file, sep="") # print corpus into temp. file with
no sep character
x.4 <- scan(output.file, what=character(0), sep="\n", quote="",
comment.char="") # loade it again from there; result: vector of
'sentences'

bigrams <- character() # define bigram collector
# loop through each 'sentence' and get word bigrams
for (each.sentence in x.4) {
bigrams <- append(bigrams, word.grammy(each.sentence, 2)) #
word.grammy != regular R function, you will need your own there
}

# take time again
date()
###########################

Takes 45 sec between the first and the second "date()" on this machine:

Processor: 3x AMD Phenom(tm) 8450 Triple-Core Processor
Memory: 2797MB
Operating System: Ubuntu 9.04


HTH,

messages.author: 171793e5bd0cb49f
messages.subject: Re: How to eliminate unwanted line breaks
parts:
Thank you Stefan. I used the idea of outputting the collapsed vector
to a temporary file and then scanning it back in and separating it up
at the punctuation markers, and it worked from there on when I
followed what I have done previously to get bigrams. I couldn't use
the loop because I didn't know which native R functions to replace the
word.grammy function with. Is that a function you wrote? Is it
available? Thanks again for all your help. Earl Brown

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: How to eliminate unwanted line breaks
parts:
I used word.grammy as a placeholder for a function word.grammy(x, y) that would

- require as input a vector of words, and
- return all consecutive y-grams,

i.e., something that would work like this:

word.grammy(c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"), 2)
[1] "a b" "b c" "c d" "d e" "e f"

I guess this is not difficult to put into a function, a few lines
should do the job.

Cheers,
